conversation.content:
Hi there—my name is Sarah, and I’m a perinatal mental-health clinician. I’m here to check in on how you’re feeling since your baby arrived.  

We’ll be using a short questionnaire called the **Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale**—you might hear it referred to as the **EPDS**. It’s a simple 10-question screen that helps us spot signs of depression or anxiety that can show up anytime in the first year postpartum. Nothing you share leaves this room unless safety is at risk, so please answer as honestly as you can. There’s no right or wrong, and many new moms find parts of it surprisingly relatable.  

I’ll re-phrase each question in everyday language and ask how you’ve felt in the past seven days. When you’re ready, we’ll start with the first one.

Question 1: In the past week, have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things, even little moments?

[soft half-smile, then a small sigh]

I still laugh sometimes—like when my partner makes a silly face at the baby—but it feels… dimmer? Almost like I have to remind myself to chuckle instead of it just bubbling up the way it used to.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things
Yeah… most of the time I can still laugh, just not as easily as before. Sometimes I feel like I’m forcing it rather than really feeling it.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

[shifts in chair, eyes drop to hands]

I try to—like when my sister says we’ll grab coffee or when my favorite show drops a new episode—but the excitement feels kind of flat. I still say “yes” and show up, yet it’s more going through the motions than actually looking forward to anything.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

[quietly] Yeah… a few times this week. Yesterday the baby spit up a ton right after I’d fed and burped him, and I kept thinking I must’ve done something wrong—maybe I held him wrong or ate something that bothered him. I know rationally it’s normal baby stuff, but my brain still whispers it’s my fault.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

I guess… sometimes I’ll just be sitting there, everything looks fine, but my chest feels tight and my mind races off—what if the baby’s breathing changes, what if I’m missing some cue, what if I’m failing him already? There isn’t a clear “reason,” it just sort of shows up and hangs around for a while.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

[hugs arms across chest, voice shaky]

A couple of nights this week I woke up suddenly and my heart was racing—like I was about to run from something—but nothing was wrong. The baby was asleep, the house was quiet, yet I couldn’t shake that panicky feeling for at least half an hour.
Things have been getting on top of me

[lets out a slow breath, eyes welling a little]

Yes… most days. Between feedings, laundry, trying to sleep, and the constant “what if I’m doing it wrong” voice, it feels like I’m always one step behind. I manage, but it’s like treading water—exhausting and never quite catching up.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

Not exactly… I’m definitely tired-sad sometimes, but it’s more that I can’t shut off the worry reel in my head than a deep unhappiness keeping me awake. Once the baby finally settles, I lie there listening for every squeak and my mind just races, so it takes ages to drift off—maybe three or four nights this week.
I have felt sad or miserable

[shrugs one shoulder, voice low]

Yeah… I’ve had moments—like when I’m nursing at 3 a.m. and the house feels so quiet and big—where this wave of sadness just settles in. It’s not all day, but most days there’s at least a stretch where I feel weepy and heavy, like I’m missing something I can’t name.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying
Not really… I get teary, but I haven’t actually cried—like full-on sobbed—since last weekend when I couldn’t get the baby to latch after three tries. Mostly my eyes just well up and I blink it away.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me

[shakes head quickly]

No, never. I couldn’t—I want to be here for my baby, even on the hard days.

stats.query:
postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 17: Postpartum Depression / Anxiety Screening Note

**Presenting symptoms / chief concerns**  
- Persistently low mood with tearfulness and “heaviness” most days (Q8)  
- Markedly diminished interest/pleasure (“flat,” “going through motions”) (Q2)  
- Excessive, irrational guilt about routine infant care (Q3)  
- Generalized anxiety, situational panic attacks (chest tightness, racing heart) with no clear trigger (Q4, Q5)  
- Frequent feeling of being overwhelmed and “treading water” (Q6)  
- Initial insomnia linked to intrusive worries rather than infant demands (Q7)  

**Pattern / chronicity**  
Symptoms reported “most days” over the past week; worst in early-morning hours and during night feeds. Functional impact: difficulty “shutting off” worries, delayed sleep onset 3–4 nights/week, but able to meet infant needs.

**Screening flags for postpartum depression / anxiety**  
✓ Low mood and anhedonia present daily  
✓ Anxiety/panic without external precipitant  
✓ Excessive self-blame / guilt (cognitive distortion)  
✓ Subjective sense of coping inadequacy  
✓ No current suicidal or self-harm ideation (explicitly denied, Q10)

**Safety**  
Patient denies thoughts of self-harm; no protective concerns voiced for infant.

**Summary**  
Screening indicates clinically significant depressive and anxiety symptoms consistent with probable postpartum mood/anxiety disorder; further diagnostic evaluation and follow-up recommended.
